title: Adjournment Motion on developing a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry in Singapore
what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion debate in which Dr Neo Kok Beng set out opportunities and proposals for a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry, and Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling responded on the Government’s approach.
why_it_matters: The transcript says drones are already used in Singapore for tasks such as ship-to-shore deliveries, tunnel and façade inspections, high-rise ledge cleaning and crowd monitoring, and that using drones for reservoir monitoring can potentially reduce required man-hours by up to 70%. It also says eVTOLs may not be viable extensively as a domestic transport option in Singapore, but could eventually be viable for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands or cross-border cargo transfer.

key_points.point: Dr Neo declared that he is the founder of an eVTOL company that designs manned drones or eVTOL in Singapore and is flying.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: I am the founder of an eVTOL company that designs manned drones or eVTOL in Singapore and is flying.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said he would explore the emerging high-growth market, set out opportunities and challenges for Singapore, and propose strategies and initiatives for building an eVTOL industry.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: I will explore this emerging and high-growth market, dissect the opportunities and challenges that we face in Singapore and propose some strategies and also what initiatives that we can have into building an eVTOL industry going forward.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said he uses the term low-altitude economy because he finds it more encompassing than advanced air mobility.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: I actually find that the low-altitude economy is more encompassing and that is why I use the terminology low-altitude economy.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said the eVTOL commercial market is projected to reach $216 billion by 2035, with a compounded annual growth rate of 51.8%.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: It is projected to reach $216 billion by 2035, with a compounded annual growth rate of 51.8%.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said Singapore could look at regional air mobility, bringing people between places such as Singapore and Johor, and Singapore and Batam.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: we can look at the air mobility business, that is, bringing people from one place to another on a regional side – Singapore and Johor, Singapore and Batam, a regional pathway that we can hop from one place to another.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said NTU's eVTOL had done its initial hover test in Singapore, but the flight trials had to be conducted in Germany.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: the trials had to be conducted in Germany forthe flight.

key_points.point: Dr Neo proposed a national initiative involving a triple helix of Government, industry, and research institutes and universities.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: We first need to have a national initiative involving a triple helix of Government, industry and of course, the research institutes and universities.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said Singapore should have a national strategy for the low-altitude economy.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: We should have a strategy, Mr Deputy Speaker, a national strategy for low-altitude economy.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said there is currently no specialisation in low-altitude mobility or advanced air mobility technology in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: Currently, there is no specialisation in such low-altitude mobility or advanced air mobility technology in Singapore.

key_points.point: Dr Neo proposed getting out of Singapore to have a regional sandbox.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: we should get out of Singapore, and therefore have a regional sandbox.

key_points.point: Dr Neo recommended that the National Research Foundation consider this a white space and allocate money for the industry, universities and research institutions.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: I would recommend that the National Research Foundation consider this to be a white space and really aggressively allocate some good money for the industry, and the universities and research institutions.

key_points.point: Dr Neo said Singapore does not design and build aircraft but has attained 10% of the world's MRO market.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: Singapore does not design and build aircraft, but we have attained 10% of the world's MRO market.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Government pays close attention to the development of the low-altitude economy.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: The Government pays close attention to the development of the low-altitude economy.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said it may not be viable to deploy eVTOLs extensively as a domestic transport option.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: Unfortunately, it may not be viable to deploy eVTOLs extensively as a domestic transport option.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said eVTOLs could eventually become viable for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands or cross-border cargo transfer with neighbouring countries.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: However, eVTOLs could eventually become a viable option for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands, or even cross-border cargo transfer with neighbouring countries.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said BCA and HDB already use drones to conduct periodic façade inspections faster and more efficiently.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: For the built environment, the Building and Construction Authority, and the Housing and Development Board already use drones to conduct periodic façade inspections in a faster and more efficient manner.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said using drones to monitor water quality and activities at reservoirs can potentially reduce required man-hours by up to 70%.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: Using drones in this manner can potentially reduce the required man-hours by up to 70%.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said CAAS facilitated initial hover tests of NTU's prototype eVTOL at the former Turf City racecourse in Kranji last year, ahead of its public unveiling at this year's Singapore Airshow.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: CAAS facilitated the initial hover tests of their prototype eVTOL at the former Turf City racecourse in Kranji last year, ahead of its public unveiling at this year’s Singapore Airshow.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Government will review how to expand testing sites, including exploring overseas sandboxes with regional neighbours.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: We will review how we can expand testing sites, including exploring overseas sandboxes in partnership with regional neighbours, as Dr Neo has suggested.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said in 2025 Singapore allowed some commercial drone operations at higher altitudes in designated areas for all days of the week for façade inspections.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: In 2025, we allowed some commercial drone operations to be conducted at higher altitudes in designated areas for all days of the week for façade inspections.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said four out of five polytechnics are approved as Unmanned Aircraft Training Organisations and conduct practical drone operations courses.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: Four out of our five polytechnics are also approved as Unmanned Aircraft Training Organisations, and conduct practical courses in drone operations.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said Singapore's airspace is limited.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: First, Singapore’s airspace is limited.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Government has generally adopted a conservative approach in the past.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: Against this backdrop, we have generally adopted a conservative approach in the past.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Government is studying overseas jurisdictions and will adapt what is relevant to Singapore's operating environment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: We are studying the approaches in overseas jurisdictions and will adapt what is relevant to Singapore’s operating environment.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said Chinese cities are trialling drones for uses including food and parcel deliveries, high-rise façade inspections, traffic monitoring and enforcement, and search and rescue, many of which Singapore may wish to explore.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: Chinese cities are trialling drones for a multitude of urban use cases, including food and parcel deliveries, high-rise façade inspections, traffic monitoring and enforcement, and search and rescue operations, many of which Singapore may also wish to explore.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Government agrees with Dr Neo on bringing together the wider ecosystem and will consult all stakeholders.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: We agree with Dr Neo that it is important to bring together the wider ecosystem and we will consult all stakeholders.

key_points.point: Ms Sun said the Ministry of Transport's immediate focus is to drive drone usage more extensively, especially by the public sector.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Transport's immediate focus is to drive the usage of drones more extensively, especially by the public sector and this is because we already have many potential use cases.

what_happens_next: The House was adjourned without question put at 6.05 pm, pursuant to the Standing Order.
not_said: Whether the Government will adopt a national strategy for the low-altitude economy, and if so, what form it would take.
Whether a dedicated sandbox or regional sandbox will be established, and where it would be located.
Whether new diploma or degree specialisations in low-altitude mobility will be introduced, and when.
Whether eVTOLs will be approved for cross-border passenger travel or cargo transfer, and under what conditions.
How potential safety, privacy and security issues from drone and eVTOL operations in dense urban areas would be addressed.
What funding, if any, the National Research Foundation might allocate to low-altitude economy research.
Whether regulations will be further changed to allow beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations or higher-altitude flights more broadly.
